card.name: edge36 hub · spoke-0 · spoke-1
card.role: one cluster manages the other two

def.what: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management, ACM, runs on a hub cluster and manages other clusters, called managed clusters or spokes.
def.creator: Clusters are registered to the hub once, at setup.
def.reader: Every controller in this video runs on either the hub or a spoke.
def.where: Hub: edge36. spoke-0: edge95. spoke-1: edge97.
def.analogy: Head office and two branch offices.

card.name: hammerdb-rhel9
card.role: the database VM we are protecting

def.what: An OpenShift Virtualization virtual machine: a full RHEL 9 guest running inside a pod.
def.creator: Created directly with oc, not from Git. That makes it a discovered application.
def.reader: KubeVirt starts it as a VirtualMachineInstance, the running copy.
def.analogy: A computer packed into a container.

card.name: hammerdb-rhel9-rootdisk
card.role: recipe that fills a VM disk

def.what: A request to the Containerized Data Importer, CDI, to create a disk and fill it, for example from an OS image.
def.creator: Created together with the VM.
def.reader: CDI creates and owns the disk claim it describes.
def.where: Namespace hammerdb. Two of them: hammerdb-rhel9-rootdisk and hammerdb-rhel9-datadisk.
def.analogy: A work order: build this disk and fill it.

card.name: hammerdb-rhel9-datadisk
card.role: the VM's claim on a real disk

def.what: A PersistentVolumeClaim, PVC, is a request for storage. It is bound to a PersistentVolume, PV, that points at a real volume on the array.
def.creator: CDI, for each DataVolume. The Dell CSI driver creates the PV and the array volume.
def.reader: The VM's pod mounts the claim as a block device.
def.analogy: A ticket stub that says which locker on the array is yours.

card.name: 52001a43-4c9e-44c2-ad24-df241b86b69d
card.role: the array copies one volume to its peer

def.what: An array-level link that copies one volume to a partner array on a schedule. One side is Source, the other is Destination.
def.creator: The Dell CSI driver, when replication is enabled for a volume.
def.reader: The arrays themselves. Kubernetes never touches the copy traffic.
def.where: Between VSA-A (spoke-0) and VSA-B (spoke-1). One session per disk.
def.analogy: A courier that ships a fresh photocopy of a folder every few minutes.

card.name: powerstore-vrc-15m
card.role: how often and with which driver to copy

def.what: A cluster-wide settings object for replication: which CSI driver, which partner array, and how often.
def.creator: Created once by the administrator on each spoke.
def.reader: csi-addons, when it enables replication for a volume.
def.analogy: The courier's contract: route and pickup schedule.

card.name: hammerdb-rhel9-rootdisk
card.role: switch: this disk is primary or secondary

def.what: A Kubernetes request to replicate one claim, with a desired role: primary (writable source) or secondary (read-only copy).
def.creator: Ramen, one per protected claim, named after the claim.
def.reader: The csi-addons controller, which calls the Dell driver over gRPC.
def.where: Namespace hammerdb, next to its claim.
def.analogy: A light switch for one disk: writable here, or copy here.

card.name: hammerdb-drpc
card.role: Ramen's site manager on one spoke

def.what: Ramen's per-cluster object for one protected app. It selects the claims, creates the VolumeReplications, and backs up definitions to S3.
def.creator: Delivered to each spoke by the Ramen hub operator.
def.reader: The Ramen cluster operator on that spoke.
def.where: Namespace openshift-dr-ops on both spokes, named hammerdb-drpc.
def.analogy: The branch manager who carries out head office orders.

card.name: ramen-metadata
card.role: off-cluster notebook both sites can read

def.what: An S3 bucket on a MinIO object store, reachable from all three clusters through the profile minio-on-hub.
def.creator: Configured once in the Ramen hub settings.
def.reader: The VRG on whichever spoke is active writes to it. The other spoke reads it during a failover.
def.analogy: A shared safe deposit box for blueprints.

card.name: openshift-adp
card.role: packs the VM's objects into S3, and unpacks them

def.what: Velero is a backup tool for Kubernetes objects. OADP is Red Hat's packaging of it, in namespace openshift-adp.
def.creator: Ramen creates Velero Backup and Restore requests on the spoke.
def.reader: Velero writes archives to the S3 bucket and restores them.
def.analogy: Movers who box up the furniture and unpack it at the new address.

def.what: A cluster-scoped hub object that pairs two clusters for disaster recovery and sets the replication interval.
def.creator: The administrator, once.
def.reader: Ramen, for every app that uses the policy.
def.analogy: The insurance policy: which two sites, how often.

card.name: hammerdb-placement
card.role: asks: which cluster runs the app?

def.what: An ACM question: which managed cluster should run this app?
def.creator: The administrator, when protecting the app.
def.reader: Normally the ACM scheduler. Here an annotation turns the scheduler off, so only Ramen answers.

def.what: The answer to a Placement: a list of cluster names.
def.creator: Ramen, because the scheduler is switched off.
def.reader: People and tools that need to know where the app should run, including the console.
def.analogy: The answer written under the question.

card.name: hammerdb-drpc
card.role: DR control panel for this app

def.what: The hub object people act on. It links the app's Placement to a DRPolicy and holds the requested action, such as Failover.
def.creator: The administrator. The console edits it when you click Failover.
def.where: Hub, namespace openshift-dr-ops, with protectedNamespaces: hammerdb.
def.analogy: The control panel with the big red button.

card.name: hammerdb-drpc-openshift-dr-ops-vrg-mw
card.role: envelope that carries an object to a spoke

def.what: An ACM delivery envelope. A hub object that contains other objects to create on one managed cluster.
def.creator: The Ramen hub operator, one per spoke.
def.reader: The work agent on that spoke, which applies the contents.
def.where: Hub, in the cluster namespaces spoke-0 and spoke-1.
def.analogy: A sealed envelope with instructions for one branch.

card.name: hammerdb-drpc-openshift-dr-ops-vrg-mcv
card.role: a window from the hub into a spoke

def.what: An ACM read-only mirror of one object on a managed cluster, refreshed into the hub.
def.creator: The Ramen hub operator, one per spoke.
def.reader: Ramen reads the VRG status through it.
def.where: Hub, in the cluster namespaces spoke-0 and spoke-1.
def.analogy: A security camera pointed at the branch's notice board.

define.text: An app deployed straight onto a cluster, not from Git. Ramen protects whole namespaces and restores objects from a Velero backup.
Ramen asks Velero to back up the namespace's Kubernetes objects to S3 on a schedule, so a discovered app can be rebuilt elsewhere.
The moment the newest copy on the other array was taken. Writes after it are not on the replica.
